rv.q: This is a ridiculously fun ride of a musical, with entertaining, outre and imaginative set-pieces.
Shearer and Leopold’s book is a lethal comedy that benefits from Seymour’s nimble direction, falling somewhere between The Producers and Titanique in tone.
It’s amusing in small doses, but the fag gibes are so relentless that they begin to verge on homophobic.
But portraying him as a sort of loveable queer rogue sells everyone short.
Here Comes J. Edgar! is a show you’ll regret missing.
The overall impression of Seymour’s chaotic yet focused staging is of a cartoon-made-flesh, and it’s irresistible.
Here Comes J Edgar! is a reminder of how difficult it is to get this right, but, mercifully, it gets there in the end.
Turns out, quite a bit. Nevertheless, we do get a lot for our money, a big show continually threatening to burst out of the confines of its snug thrust stage.
Subtitled a comedy musical, Here Comes J. Edgar Hoover succeeds brilliantly on both fronts.
This could be the most purely entertaining new musical of the year and it is surely bound for big things.
Writers Harry Shearer and Tom Leopold and director Josh Seymour have produced a gloriously funny musical out of Hoover’s life, but they have not left out his dark deeds.
This is a show that deserves to go places, and allows each performer to shine.
There is definitely much to love about Here Comes J. Edgar! but there is also the sense it could have been so much more than it currently is.
This is musical theatre at its best.

But a bit too much of it is riding on pure camp, and while it’s always entertaining and well-performed by a surprisingly large cast for a fringe venue, it doesn’t quite have the consistency to elevate it from a worth-a-look to a must-see.
Ultimately, Here Comes J. Edgar is a strong, well-executed production.

cn.t: This irreverent musical satire of FBI director J. Edgar Hoover delivers energetic laughs and witty comedy, though critics find it lightweight and one-note. Strong performances and sharp writing charm most, despite uneven execution.
